screens.label: Discussion — optional clue board
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE standalone high-resolution portrait mobile app screen mockup, not a collage or multi-screen board. Use the supplied existing IMPOSTER app screenshots as visual references only. This is a new feature design for review, not a redesign. Match the real app interior faithfully: matte charcoal #141916 background, warm ivory #F4F1E8 text, muted sage #B4C8AD secondary text, lime #D6F56B primary buttons, tiny terracotta #D98672 accents limited to established avatar colors. DM Sans-like rounded grotesk, bold 34px equivalent headlines, 16-18px body, 22px player names, 14px minimum secondary copy. Flat roster separators #343D35, round initials avatars, 16px button corners, 60px primary touch targets. Preserve the tactile stack of black/sage/terracotta secret cards with eye motifs when specified. No decorative gradients, no glass, no dashboard cards, no persistent bottom navigation, no timers, no required clue submission counter. No private secret word, hint, or role badges may appear on shared screens. Blank clues are simply absent, with no missing/awaiting labels. Frame the screen in a subtle slim black Android-style phone, straight-on, large centered display on a quiet dark studio backdrop. Small even margins around the complete phone. Phone content is the hero. No fake OS status bar, no outer captions or arrows. Keep the same framing and palette across the set. App interior is approximately 393 x 852 logical pixels; everything must fit and remain legible.
SCREEN 1: Host Alex's discussion screen, before adding his clue. Top bar: back arrow, centered "Round 3", eye icon for checking private card and QR icon at right. Large left-aligned headline "Who sounds\nsuspicious?" under the bar. Secondary copy "Talk it out. Add a clue if you like." Below, a small landscape stack of the reference secret cards, only about 90 logical pixels high, retaining the app's existing art. Then section title "Clues this round". A flat four-player roster with separators, no boxes around rows:
AL avatar in lime, "Alex · You" with a small crown, and an understated underlined action "Add my clue" below the name.
MI avatar in terracotta, "Mia", clue "Rain" below the name in readable ivory/sage.
BE avatar in muted sage, "Ben", clue "Boots" below the name.
SA avatar in sage, "Sam", with NO clue subtitle and NO missing label.
At bottom, large lime full-width button "Open voting", visibly enabled despite blank clues, then quiet text action "Pause round".
One small secondary line under the section title "Clears next round." This optional clue board replaces the existing player roster rather than creating a separate destination. Calm, spacious, real app hierarchy. No completion counts, no submission reminders, no additional calls to action.

SCREEN 3: Host Alex's voting screen after he has saved his clue. Top bar: back arrow, centered "Round 3 · Vote", eye icon and QR icon on right. Main heading "Who is the imposter?" and supporting line "Your vote stays private." Small muted sage line "Clues are locked during voting." Below, spacious ballot rows matching the supplied voting screenshot: dark flat rounded rectangles with initials avatar on left, player name and clue stacked in the middle, circular radio on right. Four rows:
MI avatar terracotta, "Mia", clue "Rain", unselected.
BE avatar sage, "Ben", clue "Boots", SELECTED with thin lime border and lime checked radio.
SA avatar sage, "Sam", no clue subtitle and no missing status, unselected.
AL avatar lime, "Alex · You", clue "Umbrella", clearly subdued and disabled to show no self-vote.
Names 22px equivalent, clues 16-18px and comfortably readable. Leave substantial breathing room under the four rows. Bottom full-width lime button "Confirm vote", enabled for selected Ben. Clues accompany each person directly so players can remember what was said while voting. NO add/edit/remove clue controls in this phase; NO public guess tally, no role or secret-word disclosure. Preserve the simple tactile, charcoal/ivory/lime app identity.
